title: Shapes and mathematical drawings quiz
description: Ten questions drawn at random from a bank of thirteen, covering inscribed polygons, constructions, bearings, scales and 3D symmetry.

questions.prompt: When constructing an inscribed regular hexagon, what must the compasses be set to?

options.text: Any width, as long as it does not change

questions.explanation: A regular hexagon is six equilateral triangles, so each side equals the radius.

questions.prompt: What is the angle at the centre of a regular octagon inscribed in a circle?

options.text: Construct $60^\circ$, bisect it, then bisect again
Construct $90^\circ$, bisect it, then bisect again

questions.prompt: Put the steps for bisecting an angle in order.

items.text: With centre at the vertex, draw an arc cutting both arms
From each of those two points, draw equal arcs that cross
Join the vertex to the crossing point

questions.explanation: The crossing point is the same distance from both arms, so the line through it splits the angle in half.

questions.prompt: In a construction, you may use a protractor to check your angles.
questions.explanation: False. A construction uses only compasses and a straight edge — no protractor and no measuring.

questions.prompt: Set the pointer to the bearing of **South-West**.
questions.explanation: South is $180^\circ$ and West is $270^\circ$. South-West is halfway: $225^\circ$.

questions.prompt: C is on a bearing of $310^\circ$ from B. What is the bearing of B from C?
A map has a scale of $1 : 50\,000$. A path is 6 cm long on the map. How long is it in real life, in km?
A ship sails on a bearing of $066^\circ$. Select **every** true statement.

options.text: It travels further East than North

questions.explanation: $066^\circ$ is between North ($000^\circ$) and East ($090^\circ$), and closer to East, so the ship goes North and East, with more East than North.

questions.prompt: A ship ends up 20 km East and 10 km South of port. Find the bearing it sailed on, to the nearest degree.
questions.explanation: The line is $27^\circ$ South of due East. East is $090^\circ$, so the bearing is $090^\circ + 27^\circ = 117^\circ$ (a scale drawing gives about $116^\circ$–$118^\circ$).

questions.prompt: How many planes of symmetry does a regular pentagonal prism have?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 lines of symmetry, giving 5 planes, plus 1 across the middle: 6.

questions.prompt: Which shape has exactly 9 planes of symmetry?

options.text: A cuboid with all edges different
A square-based prism 2 cm × 2 cm × 7 cm

questions.explanation: A cube has 3 + 6 = 9. The cuboid has 3, the square prism has 5 and the cylinder has infinitely many.

questions.prompt: The perpendicular bisector of the diameter AB is used to construct an inscribed square. Click the part of the circle that AB is.
questions.explanation: AB runs from one side of the circle to the other through the centre, so it is a **diameter**. Its perpendicular bisector is a second diameter at right angles, giving the four corners of the square.
